clue.text: Coach right to oppose racial stirring

indicators.note: the abbreviation is set against, standing in front of, the reworked letters
stirring mixes things up, so the letters of racial are jumbled

explanation.surface: A coach, or trainer, encourages someone to stand up against racist agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a verb about training, but it is a railway carriage; 'to oppose' sets R against, in front of, the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage is called a coach, and a self-propelled passenger carriage is the same kind of vehicle.

indicators.note: mid- points to the central letter of the nine-letter word afternoon
the word tea is broken up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone prices up a mid-afternoon tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-' takes the centre letter of AFTERNOON, R; 'break' rearranges TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To value something is to assess or estimate its worth, a direct synonym.

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Muslims

explanation.surface: Someone introduces themselves as a Muslim religious leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads prayers in a mosque, so the whole clue is the speaker describing his role.

parts.note: the phrase reads like a description of futile effort, but describes flirtatious behaviour aimed at attracting men

explanation.surface: Someone tries without success to catch a man's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vainly' suggests 'without success', but here it means 'out of vanity'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flirtation by a woman who wants admiration from men is the classic sense of this word.

clue.text: Check the key in, as a rule

indicators.note: the key is placed in the middle of the word for check

parts.note: to rein in a horse is to check it
G is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Someone checks the key has been put in the lock, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like 'usually', but 'rule' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is a period of rule, so the noun means the same as rule.

indicators.note: the word for paper holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: card is stiff paper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper carries a baseless piece of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' suggests a newspaper, but it is CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or hoax spread as news.

clue.text: Barber's work is to be performed slowly

definitions.meaning: Samuel Barber's best-known piece is his ... for Strings
the musical tempo marking for a slow pace

explanation.surface: Someone says a hairdresser's work must be done at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barber' is not a hairdresser but the American composer Samuel Barber.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer's famous work is named by its tempo, and the Italian marking means at a slow pace.

clue.text: It is beyond the directors to be honest

parts.note: above means beyond, as in above one's station
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Honesty is something the company's directors cannot manage.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealings that are open and legitimate are called above board, an idiom for honest.

clue.text: You can have it, yet still be clothes-mad

definitions.text: You can have it, yet still be clothes-mad

parts.words: You can have it, yet still be clothes-mad
parts.note: mad is read as lacking sense, so one can be obsessed with clothes and still have good taste in them

explanation.surface: A fashion obsessive may still possess a certain quality.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'clothes-mad' suggests no sense, yet the phrase names a sense for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A knack for choosing and wearing clothes well is what this phrase names.

clue.text: Snuggled into a new quilt, managed to remain undisturbed

indicators.note: one piece settles inside the other like a sleeper inside bedding
the letters of quilt are made new by rearranging them

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone tucked into a fresh duvet manages to stay asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snuggled into' suggests going under the duvet; here one piece simply sits inside the jumbled other, splitting off its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and peaceful, with nothing to disturb it, is the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Take cover when one is after a gangster

indicators.note: the word one comes after the word for cover

parts.note: a cap is a head covering or a lid
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes shelter while a hoodlum is pursuing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is after' looks like being chased but simply orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era.

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
on means supported by, as in living on bread

explanation.surface: A stray dog is kept alive on scraps of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh of a mature sheep eaten as food is this meat.

definitions.meaning: to be in earnest about one's intentions
usury, lending at high interest, is jokingly read as a stingy or mean trade

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to take moneylending seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the idiom literally: mean (stingy) business, a fair description of usury.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be serious, and read literally it describes a miserly trade such as usury.

parts.note: read not as a flute or horn but as a device that measures wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind instrument' suggests a musical instrument, but this one measures wind speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological device that gauges wind speed is literally an instrument for wind.

clue.text: Part of a shirt and collar

definitions.meaning: the slit a button passes through
to collar someone is to waylay them for a talk

explanation.surface: A shirt's component and its neckband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' looks like a second part of a shirt, but it is the verb meaning to accost.
explanation.definitionFit: The slit for a button is part of a shirt, and to detain someone in talk is the verb sense of collar.

clue.text: Country's position that's not in dispute

definitions.text: Country's position that's not in dispute

parts.words: Country's position that's not in dispute
parts.note: reads like an agreed fact, but describes a nation's stance of staying out of conflicts

explanation.surface: A nation's uncontested status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in dispute' seems to mean undisputed, but means not taking part in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A state that takes no side in a war holds this status, like Switzerland.

indicators.note: an assortment is a mix, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A small mixed collection of creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment of' rearranges A SMALL.
explanation.definitionFit: South American pack animals related to camels are an example of animals.

indicators.note: recitation means speaking aloud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: money due is owed

explanation.surface: A poem is set for someone to recite.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric poem addressed to a subject, often in elevated style, is this kind of poem.

indicators.note: the hour abbreviation goes inside the word for plough

parts.note: a tiller is a machine that tills or ploughs the soil
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Someone reserves an hour at the pub called the Plough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, and 'the Plough' like a pub (a common British pub name), but they are a novel and a tiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspenseful novel is called a thriller, an example of a book.

definitions.meaning: to have ... a challenge is to have faced it

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to London's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing up to something is meeting it, and London's police force is known as the Met.

parts.note: rousing is read literally as waking people up, and the performers are birds

explanation.surface: A stirring open-air concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rousing' suggests stirring, but it means waking sleepers at daybreak.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong at daybreak is the early-morning singing that wakes sleepers.

clue.text: I get in trouble, but make light of the matter

indicators.note: the letters are troubled, that is stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in a scrape tries to laugh it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges I GET IN; 'make light of the matter' means set the stuff alight, not belittle it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set fire to a substance is to kindle it, a literal reading of making the matter alight.

clue.text: Could be a more teasing sexual arrangement

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A flirtatious arrangement between lovers that might be more provocative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges A MORE TEASING.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic set-up in which three people share a sexual relationship is this French phrase.

definitions.meaning: plump as an adjective means ... and chubby
a set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: Choose to buy drinks for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' looks like the verb 'choose', but 'Plump' is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump means chubby, a synonym of rounded, and a set of drinks for the group is bought as a single order.

parts.note: sewers is read not as drains but as people who sew, so the case holds needles

explanation.surface: A matter for the drainage system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewers' looks like drains, but means people who sew.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental needle case is the word, an old French term.

parts.note: the word names a small Scottish island and also a tiny length, so it could hardly be long

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at New York's Long Island.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland the word is a small island, and as a unit of length it is barely long at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island in Scottish place names bears this name, and it is also a short length.

clue.text: Subject matter about right for a mundane circle

indicators.note: the word for subject matter goes about, around, the other piece

parts.note: a topic is the subject matter of a discussion

explanation.surface: A dull talk about a correct but boring topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mundane' here means earthly: a line of latitude circling the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Either of the two lines of latitude round the Earth is a circle on the world, mundane meaning worldly.

parts.note: loaded is read as a gun with a round in it, and statement as a news announcement

explanation.surface: A remark full of hidden meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is a bullet in, as in a loaded gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A short official news announcement is a statement, and split in two it describes a loaded gun.

indicators.note: the letters are arranged unusually, in a new order

explanation.surface: Magistrates of old were remarkably harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges SEVERE.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England these officials were local magistrates or stewards.

clue.text: He needs religious ecstasy to fuel his whirling

definitions.text: He needs religious ecstasy to fuel his whirling

parts.words: He needs religious ecstasy to fuel his whirling
parts.note: describes a Sufi mystic whose spinning dance is driven by religious fervour

explanation.surface: A spinning figure is powered by spiritual rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirling' is the giveaway: Sufi mystics known for spinning in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi Muslim ascetic famous for ecstatic whirling dances is meant.
